content: Methenamine is an antibiotic that works by eliminating bacteria responsible for urinary tract infections (UTIs). It is typically prescribed for long-term use to manage chronic infections and to prevent the recurrence of such infections. However, it is important to note that antibiotics, including methenamine, are ineffective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Methenamine is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is usually taken either twice daily (every 12 hours) or four times daily (after meals and at bedtime). Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take methenamine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Swallow the coated tablets whole; do not crush or break them. Take the tablets with a full glass of water or with food. If you are using the liquid form, shake it well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Before taking methenamine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to methenamine, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and medications), or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially antacids, sulfamethizole, diuretics (commonly known as water pills), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking methenamine, contact your doctor immediately. Methenamine may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Methenamine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach cramps, or loss of appetite. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash, hives, or itching (indicative of an allergic reaction). If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store methenamine in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to methenamine. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
